title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. A fabricated video was branded with the logo of an established news outlet and built around a fake clip of that outlet's editor-in-chief, so the deception worked by borrowing the credibility of a real publication rather than by exploiting a flaw in a model or a system. It happened at the point of distribution on a social platform, where the post circulated under an account name and accumulated views before anyone at the outlet saw it.

Catching it required the outlet itself to notice and confirm the video was fake, and its lawyer to complain to the platform, which then removed the post on a trademark ground rather than on the basis of the false claim. Nothing in the reporting describes a pre-publication check, a provenance signal, or a platform detection step that flagged the video as synthetic before it spread. The gap is that the only party positioned to identify the forgery was the party being impersonated.

The reporting attributes the video to a named Russian disinformation campaign and describes earlier deepfakes of celebrities in the same operation. It is not established that the account named роман is connected to the Russian state, that the campaign changed any vote, or that the platform's removal was motivated by the disinformation rather than the trademark complaint.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A fake Mother Jones video circulated on X, posted by an account named роман, claiming the Democratic National Committee paid CNN chief Mark Thompson $259 million to promote gender transition among children. The video, falsely branded with a Mother Jones logo and featuring a fake clip of editor-in-chief Clara Jeffery, drew 155,000 views on one account and 50,000 on another within a day. Mother Jones confirmed the video was fake, and its lawyer complained to X, which removed the post for a trademark violation.

The video is part of a Russian disinformation campaign called Storm-1679 or Matryoshka, which has spread fake CNN and other news reports, including deepfakes of celebrities urging votes for Republicans. The operation, first identified by the group @antibot4navalny, has targeted the 2026 midterms and previously interfered in 2024. The article says the campaign has not yet gained major reach, but warns that Trump has shut down federal units that once tracked Russian disinformation.
